selected.title: The room that watches itself
selected.texas_link: Houston Methodist Hospital ran the system in its 15 room cardiothoracic operating suite at Walter Tower in Houston. The film draws a generic operating room as an illustration and shows no real room, staff member or patient.

movement.action: published an observational study of camera based AI in an operating suite
movement.object: Apella image based AI cameras in the Walter Tower cardiothoracic suite

selected.why_today: The Docket record on the study is current and the hospital's own August 14th, 2026 blog repeats the result and adds that turnover times decreased, a claim the peer reviewed paper does not evaluate, so the film keeps that open.
selected.consequence: Surgeons receive a text when a patient is draped, and the suite shows about 25 more cases a month that the authors say are associated with the rollout rather than caused by it.
selected.application_change: Operating room events such as patient draping that had never been captured before are timestamped from camera images, and surgeons are texted at the draping event.
selected.counter_image: The rollout was bundled with other workflow changes, the placebo test did not reach conventional significance, the hospital holds a minority stake in the vendor, and the paper left turnover time for future work even though the hospital's blog says turnover decreased.
selected.earned_take: The cameras log the room and text the surgeon, and the paper can't say they added the cases.

agency.next_step: The authors say future work should assess turnover time and whether the case volume gain holds across other surgical specialties.
agency.who_can_act: Houston Methodist researchers and operating room leaders can run that follow up, and other hospitals can test their own rooms.

sources.note: Nguyen and colleagues, Journal of Imaging, open access, full text via Europe PMC, published online June 27th, 2026
Houston Methodist blog of August 14th, 2026 describing the same system

filmability.viewer_question: Does a camera that logs an operating room add surgeries, or only count them?
filmability.opening_action: An illustrated wall camera in a generic operating room stamps the moment a patient is wheeled in, disclosed as Illustration.
filmability.mechanism: Input: images from four cameras in each room. Transformation: a model timestamps patient entry, draping and turnover. Result: the surgeon gets a text at draping. Limit: the study measured case volume, not turnover, and calls the rise associated rather than caused.
filmability.human_consequence: Surgeons are texted when a patient is draped, and staff raised surveillance and privacy concerns according to the hospital. No person is named or drawn.
filmability.source_limit: Observational study, bundled rollout, placebo test short of conventional significance, hospital equity in the vendor and a vendor employee who ran the original analyses. The hospital blog says turnover times decreased but the paper did not evaluate turnover. No footage of the real room is cleared, so the room is an authored illustration.
three_key_images: An illustrated wall camera stamping patient entry on a room clock in a generic operating room
An illustrated draping event with a text alert arriving on a phone
A record card reading about 25 more cases a month beside the words associated, not caused, and the interval 8.3 to 41.0

asset_leads.relevant_image: Paper figures 1, 3, 4 and 5 carry Apella's written CC BY permission
asset_leads.what_it_proves: Camera placement and an event timeline, per captions only
asset_leads.rights_basis: CC BY 4.0 per the article, but consent notes say some faces are vendor generic images, so no figure is admitted.
All rights reserved, no licence stated.

action_support.pictured_action: An illustrated wall camera stamps a patient being wheeled into a generic operating room on a room clock.
action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed illustration of the paper's detected entry event. It shows no real room, vendor interface or person.
action_support.relationship: The paper says the system detected patient entry, draping and room turnover.

action_support.pictured_action: The drape goes over an illustrated patient shape and an event marker lands on the room clock without second level times.
action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed illustration of the draping event. No timing precision is shown.
action_support.relationship: The paper records a Patient Draped event between anesthesia ready and case start.

action_support.pictured_action: A text alert arrives on an illustrated phone at the draping event, then a record card reads about 25 more cases a month, associated and not caused.
action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed illustration of the text event and the paper's estimate. The surgeon's reaction is not pictured.
action_support.relationship: The paper says automated text notifications informed surgeons when patients were draped.

visual_stakes.affected_group: Surgeons and operating room staff at the Walter Tower cardiothoracic suite.
visual_stakes.physical_subject: a wall camera, a room clock with event markers and a surgeon's phone
visual_stakes.visible_change: the patient entry and draping events are stamped on the room clock and a text alert reaches the surgeon's phone
visual_stakes.consequence: about 25 more cases a month that the authors say are associated with the rollout, not caused by it
visual_stakes.opening_question: Does a camera that logs an operating room add surgeries, or only count them?
visual_stakes.answer: The study finds about 25 more cases a month and can't say the cameras caused them.
visual_stakes.asset_fit: Authored illustration only. No photographs are admitted, so no rights are in question.
visual_stakes.affected_person: No person is drawn. Staff appear only as a phone alert and an event clock, disclosed as illustration.
